Subject: Re: MAP acceptance criteria — unit economics and eval steps

Hi Alex — quick response and plan below.

Short answers (for procurement):
- Baseline unit cost: $0.0075 / 1k tokens (hosted canonical model used in pilot)
- Avg tokens per flow: 420 tokens (inbound prompt + generated content)
- Effective tokens/$: ~133k tokens per $1 at baseline
- Caching: prefix KV caching on conversational threads; typical reduction 12-20% on
  question/answer flows after warmup (we model 15% conservatively)
- Batching: small micro-batches (batch size 4–8) for low-latency routes, larger
  batching for background bulk evals; throughput-optimized batches increase
  tokens/sec by ~2.1x but add 30–80ms tail latency per request.

Attached: redwood_unit_econ_model_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet) — has the math and a
sensitivity table (prefetch 0/10/20% and batch sizes 1/4/16).

Proposed eval plan and timeline (high level):
1) Wed 26 May — Redwood provides token trace simulator and updated econ sheet
2) Thu 27 May — Carebridge runs 24h traffic sample and returns actual token
   distribution
3) Fri 28 May — Redwood runs simulated MAP using Carebridge sample and emits
   pass/fail gate on (avg tokens/$, 95th perc latency)
4) Mon 31 May — Finalize SOW/Purchase Order

If procurement prefers we can provide a short addendum to the SOW with the
three gating numbers we recommend (baseline tokens/$, caching delta, latency
SLO). Let me know procurement contact and we will send the addendum.

Thanks,
Dylan

--

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: MAP acceptance criteria — unit economics and eval steps

Following up with more technical detail to feed into the MAP checklist:

- Token distribution assumptions: pilot used median prompt 68 tokens inbound,
  generated 352 tokens on average (skewed by long summaries). If you have a
  heavy short-interaction use case, swap in the 25th perc numbers in the sheet.
- Cache warmup: KV cache shows diminishing returns over 12–24h; first-time
  interactions see no benefit. For SOW we recommend modeling a warmup window of
  48 hours for active cohorts.
- Prefetch strategy: for predictable flows (e.g., appointment summaries) we
  recommend prefetching likely next-turn prompts which reduces end-to-end
  tokens by ~18% in our sim. See sheet (prefetch tab).
- Batching latency math: for microbatching at batch=4, expect ~10–35ms added
  P99 tail from queuing under nominal load; at batch=16 it's ~120–220ms.

Simulator note: the attached sim_results_5_23.csv contains two traffic
profiles (weekday/light and weekend/heavy) and the modeled tokens/$ across
varying batch sizes and cache hit rates. We used GPU A100 equivalent pricing
in the baseline.

If procurement needs a single-line statement: "Redwood projects baseline
unit-cost at $0.0075/1k tokens with a modeled 15% caching reduction and
batching tradeoffs per attached sensitivity table."

-ben
